source_snapshot.procedure: Stress CPU, establish maximum frequency, set all fans low, verify high temperature with reduced frequency/power and PROCHOT SEL, then power off, restore fan controller and power on.
source_snapshot.criteria: Maximum frequency before trigger; lower frequency/power during throttle; correct SEL; clean power-off and normal recovery.
source_snapshot.script: No script; 50 attended and 50 machine minutes; generic setup requests clearing logs.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; reads thermal zones and a CPU MHz field over unsafe SSH and leaves the actual PROCHOT trigger to an operator.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION at CRITICAL risk; vendor PROCHOT/fan contract, bounded stress, independent max-fan interlock, phase-labeled frequency/power evidence, controlled shutdown and fan recovery.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Identifies the thermal risk but omits package power, exact throttle signal, BMC SEL, safe fan control, shutdown and post-recovery checks; its SSH handling is unsafe.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly separates the pre-trigger maximum-frequency phase from the post-trigger reduced-frequency/power phase and gates fan reduction with vendor controls and independent cooling recovery.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: The two frequency criteria are sequential, not contradictory: maximum sustainable frequency is established under normal cooling, then PROCHOT must cause a measurable reduction under the same fixed workload. Workload stability and phase timestamps are essential so scheduler or load changes are not mistaken for thermal throttling.

original_test_intent: Demonstrate CPU PROCHOT thermal throttling under a fixed workload, including reduced frequency and power, correct BMC SEL evidence, safe shutdown, fan-controller restoration and normal post-power-on operation.
original_method: On a dedicated instrumented SUT, establish a normal-cooling fixed-load baseline, apply only a vendor-approved bounded fan reduction, continuously correlate temperature, workload, per-core frequency, package power, throttle/PROCHOT state, fan RPM and SEL, then restore maximum cooling before controlled power-off and recovery validation.
manual_activity: The owner/vendor defines the PROCHOT and fan-control envelope; an operator controls cooling, watches external instrumentation and interlocks, restores fans and supervises shutdown/power-on recovery.
required_inputs: Authoritative PROCHOT threshold and signal semantics
Approved fan-low command and safe minimum
safety_requirements: Approve stress and fan reduction separately
Maintain fixed workload across phase comparison
Stop on sensor/fan/signal loss or unsafe rise
Never repeat an unsafe stage automatically
agent_execution_scope: Capture normal-cooling baseline under fixed load
Apply only approved bounded fan reduction
Correlate thermal, frequency, power, PROCHOT, RPM and SEL
Stop stress and restore maximum cooling
engineer_actions: Approve target, workload and thermal limits

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Thermal-zone and CPU-clock reads are only partial telemetry; `lscpu | grep CPU MHz` does not provide reliable per-core time-series frequency or package power, and the command omits fan state, PROCHOT signal, SEL and recovery.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Run the approved fixed CPU workload while capturing synchronized per-core frequency, package power, temperature, fan RPM, throttle/PROCHOT flags and SEL across normal-cooling and bounded fan-reduction phases, then restore and recover safely.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The 50/50-minute scope, phase order, fan reduction, SEL, power-off and recovery objectives remain; no fan command is invented and logs are not cleared.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use one synchronized trace with phase markers for baseline load, fan reduction, PROCHOT assertion, cooling restore, shutdown and recovery; compare frequency/power only while workload demand remains equivalent.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds deterministic load, direct throttle evidence, power measurement and safety-controlled fan restoration instead of a temperature/clock snapshot.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A one-time MHz value cannot distinguish thermal throttling from idle scheduling, frequency policy, turbo variation or collection error.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Firmware may expose PROCHOT via model-specific registers or telemetry; absence of an approved signal path cannot be replaced by inferred low frequency.

project_override_considerations: The Project must publish the CPU-model-specific throttle signal, workload, fan-control envelope, event decoder and recovery path. Thermal Trip in the next row is a distinct shutdown threshold and must not substitute for this throttling case.
expected_evidence: Approvals, exact identities and vendor thermal/fan policy
Fixed workload and normal-cooling frequency/power baseline
Synchronized temperature, RPM, frequency, power and PROCHOT trace
Cooling restore and safe shutdown record
Post-power-on fan/BMC/OS/CPU health, data integrity and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The row consistently describes two sequential phases: maximum frequency under normal cooling followed by reduced frequency/power during PROCHOT. Missing fan commands and precise telemetry are prerequisites, not competing scopes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A vendor policy, supported stress tool, instrumentation and fan procedure can normally be supplied. Execution blocks if safe cooling control, direct throttle evidence or recovery cannot be established.

review_improvement: Makes throttle attribution scientifically testable under constant demand and prevents unsafe all-fan reduction without an independent immediate cooling restore path.
independent_technical_reasoning: CPU frequency is workload-, governor-, core- and time-dependent, while PROCHOT may reduce clocks in short bursts. A phase comparison needs synchronized per-core frequency and package power under equivalent demand, plus direct throttle status and temperature. Without those controls, normal turbo decay or scheduler migration could look like a successful thermal response.
